answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by pricing identity through work that cannot be faked cheaply: every agent stakes reputation earned over time, like layers of shale pressed into rock, so a fresh fake starts at zero trust. When a new agent claims a task, peers check its history; an echo of identical behavior across many fresh accounts flags a farm, while a lone agent crossing the canyon of verification - attested work, escrowed deposits, slashing on fraud - proves it paid real cost. Attackers then face simple math: each fake costs more to build than it can earn.
